title: Economic Power in International Trade
abstract: arXiv:2607.09990v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Economic power is a country's capacity to harm another more than itself by withdrawing from a trading relationship. This paper develops a general equilibrium model of the world trade network to measure that power through counterfactual sanctions. Using a world input-output table of eighty economies and fifty industries, we solve for $3{,}160$ such sanction equilibria, one for each bilateral severance of a trading relationship. We read the asymmetry between the two sides' losses as power. Our results show that mutual trade dependence is anything but mutual. The distribution of power in world trade is highly skewed. In the median trade relationship, one country inflicts on its trading partner more than four times the loss it bears. Only one pair in seven is close to balanced. translated_title: 国际贸易中的经济权力
translated_abstract: 经济权力是指一个国家通过退出贸易关系而使对方受到的伤害大于自身所受伤害的能力。本文构建了一个世界贸易网络的一般均衡模型，通过反事实制裁来衡量这种权力。利用包含八十个经济体和五十个行业的世界投入产出表，我们求解了3,160个此类制裁均衡，每一个均衡对应一种双边贸易关系的切断。我们将双方损失之间的不对称性解读为权力。我们的结果表明，所谓的相互贸易依赖绝非相互对等：世界贸易中的权力分布高度偏斜，在中位数的贸易关系中，一国对其贸易伙伴造成的损失超过其自身所承受损失的四倍，只有七分之一的贸易对接近平衡。美国比其全部79个伙伴都更强大，而中国除一个伙伴外也比所有其他伙伴更强大。经济权力并非由双边贸易……
tldr: 本文通过构建世界贸易网络的一般均衡模型并求解3,160个反事实制裁均衡，揭示了世界贸易中经济权力分布高度不对称：中位数贸易关系中一方对伙伴造成的损失超过自身损失的四倍，且美国和中国几乎对所有贸易伙伴都拥有权力优势。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a general equilibrium model of the world trade network and solves 3,160 counterfactual sanction equilibria, revealing that economic power in world trade is highly skewed—in the median relationship one country inflicts more than four times its own loss on its partner, with the United States more powerful than all 79 partners and China more powerful than all but one.
